Exact sampler design: construct each user’s exclusions from all distinct training positives plus padding. For sparse users, uniformly draw catalog IDs, rejecting exclusions and previously accepted negatives; this gives uniform sampling without replacement, but slows as the eligible pool shrinks. For dense users, cache the sorted eligible complement and use `rng.choice(complement, k, replace=False)` with no probability weights. NumPy documents uniform sampling without replacement through this interface. Require `k <= eligible_count`; never silently introduce duplicates. [NumPy choice](https://numpy.org/doc/1.17/reference/random/generated/numpy.random.Generator.choice.html). An inferred memory-saving alternative: sample distinct ranks from the eligible population, then map ranks to catalog IDs using sorted exclusions and binary search; the bijection preserves uniformity without materializing the complement.

For reproducibility, provide an explicitly seeded `torch.Generator` to DataLoader and initialize worker-local Python/NumPy RNGs from `torch.initial_seed()`; independently created NumPy generators need explicit initialization. PyTorch assigns worker seeds using `base_seed + worker_id`. [DataLoader documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html), [reproducibility guidance](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/randomness.md). Checkpoint Python, NumPy, CPU/CUDA Torch RNG states, the DataLoader generator, and sampler progress alongside model/optimizer state. Main-process RNG restoration alone cannot reconstruct prefetched batches or persistent workers’ evolving RNG states. A practical design inference is to derive negative-sampling seeds deterministically from training seed, epoch, user/sample ID, and occurrence index; this removes dependence on worker scheduling. Exact mid-epoch resume additionally requires restoring sample order and the consumed position, or explicitly preserving loader state.
